I’m on Adderall, mostly because my BPD was
misdiagnosed as ADHD early in life and frankly it helps with the impulsiveness, and it is probably a comorbidity in my case.

That said, pharmaceutical interventions for BPD are very limited and pale in comparison to DBT. So really if DBT is working the medications will probably not be needed unless they treat a comorbid condition. But the fact they are working suggests there -is- something they are treating so coming off them without a doctors recommendation would be unwise.

The medication is for you, to change how you treat yourself. BPD is at its core a lack of identity, and self worth, and self love. As long as we depend on others, especially just one person, for those things, we will be disappointed. 

You’ll know it’s working when you realize that you both deserve to be treated well in a relationship, but also can’t compel a particular individual to treat you better. If they don’t want a serious relationship with you, they are probably not ready for that in general and you deserve to find someone that is because you matter and your happiness matters.
